# Add the following to your dataframe:

-Total sentences (use nltk sentence parser)

	Identify future-oriented sentences by looking for future oriented words

-FOG

-Total complex words (for the whole doc and for future tense)   >3 syllables

-Total Future Sentences

-Every variable/column should have a future version (this doubles the number of columns, e.g. positivity and future_positivity)


**Future oriented words:**
Will/
Shall/
May/
Might/
Should/
*Going to

%pip -q install beautifulsoup4 nltk syllables

import os
import re
import glob
import pandas as pd
import nltk
import syllables
from collections import Counter
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from nltk.tokenize import sent_tokenize

nltk.download('punkt_tab', quiet=True) #下载nltk识别句子所需的材料,quiet隐藏细节信息

downloadDir = "/content/drive/MyDrive/Text_Mining/Temp10-Ks/"
dictionaryFile = "/content/drive/MyDrive/Text_Mining/Loughran-McDonald_MasterDictionary.csv"
cmuFile = "/content/drive/MyDrive/Text_Mining/cmudict.txt"

threshold = 3 #minimum syllables to view as complex

lm = pd.read_csv(dictionaryFile)
lm["Word"] = lm["Word"].astype(str).str.lower()

positiveWords = set(lm.loc[lm["Positive"] > 0, "Word"])
negativeWords = set(lm.loc[lm["Negative"] > 0, "Word"])
litigiousWords = set(lm.loc[lm["Litigious"] > 0, "Word"])

print("Positive words:", len(positiveWords))
print("Negative words:", len(negativeWords))
print("Litigious words:", len(litigiousWords))

futurePattern = re.compile(r"\b(will|shall|may|might|should)\b|\bgoing\s+to\b", re.I)

# example：
example = "The firm earned revenue. The firm may expand next year."
print([sentence for sentence in sent_tokenize(example) if futurePattern.search(sentence)])

textFiles = glob.glob(downloadDir + "*.txt")
results = []

if len(textFiles) == 0:
    raise FileNotFoundError("No 10-K .txt files found. Check downloadDir.")

for textFile in textFiles:
    #  Read one 10-K
    with open(textFile, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f:
        rawText = f.read()

    # ② Remove HTML tags before text analysis
    soup = BeautifulSoup(rawText, "html.parser")
    for tag in soup(["script", "style"]):
        tag.decompose()
    text = soup.get_text(separator=" ", strip=True)

    # ③ Split into sentences
    sentences = sent_tokenize(text)
    totalSentences = len(sentences)

    # ④ Find future-oriented sentences
    futureSentences = []
    for sentence in sentences:
        if futurePattern.search(sentence):
            futureSentences.append(sentence)
    totalFutureSentences = len(futureSentences)

    # ⑤ Word counts for the FULL 10-K (same approach as Week 3)
    words = re.findall(r"[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?", text.lower())
    wordCount = len(words)
    wordCounter = Counter(words)

    positiveCount = sum(wordCounter[word] for word in positiveWords)
    negativeCount = sum(wordCounter[word] for word in negativeWords)
    litigiousCount = sum(wordCounter[word] for word in litigiousWords)

    positivityRate = positiveCount / wordCount if wordCount else 0
    negativityRate = negativeCount / wordCount if wordCount else 0
    litigiousRate = litigiousCount / wordCount if wordCount else 0

    complexCount = sum(syllableCount(word) > threshold for word in words)
    fog = 0.4 * (wordCount / totalSentences + 100 * complexCount / wordCount) if wordCount and totalSentences else 0

    # ⑥ Repeat calculations for FUTURE sentences only
    futureText = " ".join(futureSentences).lower()
    futureWords = re.findall(r"[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)?", futureText)
    futureWordCount = len(futureWords)
    futureCounter = Counter(futureWords)

    futurePositiveCount = sum(futureCounter[word] for word in positiveWords)
    futureNegativeCount = sum(futureCounter[word] for word in negativeWords)
    futureLitigiousCount = sum(futureCounter[word] for word in litigiousWords)

    futurePositivityRate = futurePositiveCount / futureWordCount if futureWordCount else 0
    futureNegativityRate = futureNegativeCount / futureWordCount if futureWordCount else 0
    futureLitigiousRate = futureLitigiousCount / futureWordCount if futureWordCount else 0

    futureComplexCount = sum(syllableCount(word) > threshold for word in futureWords)
    futureFog = 0.4 * (futureWordCount / totalFutureSentences + 100 * futureComplexCount / futureWordCount) if futureWordCount and totalFutureSentences else 0

    # ⑦ Save one row (same as Week 3: results.append)
    results.append([
        os.path.basename(textFile),
        wordCount, positiveCount, negativeCount, litigiousCount,
        positivityRate, negativityRate, litigiousRate,
        totalSentences, complexCount, fog, totalFutureSentences,
        futureWordCount, futurePositiveCount, futureNegativeCount,
        futureLitigiousCount, futurePositivityRate, futureNegativityRate,
        futureLitigiousRate, totalFutureSentences, futureComplexCount, futureFog
    ])

print("Processed", len(results), "10-K files")

df = pd.DataFrame(results, columns=[
    "filename", "wordCount", "PositiveWordCount", "NegativeWordCount",
    "LitigiousWordCount", "PositivityRate", "NegativityRate", "LitigiousRate",
    "TotalSentences", "TotalComplexWords", "FOG", "TotalFutureSentences",
    "future_wordCount", "future_PositiveWordCount", "future_NegativeWordCount",
    "future_LitigiousWordCount", "future_PositivityRate", "future_NegativityRate",
    "future_LitigiousRate", "future_TotalSentences", "future_TotalComplexWords", "future_FOG"
])

display(df.head())
print("Rows and columns:", df.shape)

outputFile = "/content/drive/MyDrive/Text_Mining/week4_results.csv"
df.to_csv(outputFile, index=False)
print("Saved to:", outputFile)
